drafts.email1:
Hi Francois,

I came across NCT07284472 — your Phase 2, Phase 3 study of EXV-802, Placebo in Agitation Associated With Alzheimer's Disease Dementia, and wanted to reach out.

Phase 2 is where the exposure-response relationship defines the programme's trajectory — a robust E-R model at this stage directly supports the Phase 3 dose rationale and significantly reduces regulatory back-and-forth. With 300 patients, you'll have a dataset that supports a strong PopPK/PD model, and getting that analysis right now is often the difference between a clean Phase 3 dose rationale and a regulatory back-and-forth that delays the pivotal trial. For EXV-802, Placebo, getting this analysis right now avoids costly protocol amendments downstream.

Our team at PumasAI — pharmacometricians and clinical pharmacologists, several from FDA, Pfizer, and BMS — has delivered 40+ regulatory submissions across FDA, EMA, PMDA, and Health Canada, all accepted on first review. We handle the full clinical pharmacology programme end-to-end: PopPK, exposure-response, dose optimisation, clinical trial simulation, and regulatory writing through submission.

Would a short call make sense to see if there's a fit? Happy to share a relevant case study from a similar Phase 2, Phase 3 Neurology programme beforehand.

drafts.email1:
Hi Richard,

I came across NCT06993142 — your study of Increase of physical activity volume and intensity with the use of a motivational smartphone application in Parkinson Disease, Prodromal Stage, and wanted to reach out.

Programmes like this benefit significantly from building model-informed drug development into the clinical strategy early — whether it's PK/PD characterisation for Increase of physical activity volume and intensity with the use of a motivational smartphone application, exposure-response for efficacy endpoints in Parkinson Disease, Prodromal Stage, or simulation-based dose optimisation for special populations. With 600 patients, having a regulatory-ready quantitative package that addresses FDA and EMA expectations upfront avoids the back-and-forth that often delays timelines.

Our team at PumasAI — pharmacometricians and clinical pharmacologists, several from FDA, Pfizer, and BMS — has delivered 40+ regulatory submissions across FDA, EMA, PMDA, and Health Canada, all accepted on first review. We handle the full clinical pharmacology programme end-to-end: NCA, PopPK, exposure-response, dose justification, and regulatory writing through submission.

I also noticed Cure Parkinson's has active programmes in Immunology & Inflammation/Neurology (Phase 2) and Neurology/Oncology (Phase 3) — if there's a clinical pharmacology need on any of those fronts, happy to discuss.

Would a short call make sense to see if there's a fit? Happy to share a relevant case study from a similar Dermatology programme beforehand.
drafts.subject2: Re: NCT06993142 — MIDD & Clinical Pharmacology Support
drafts.fu1:
Hi Richard,

Wanted to follow up briefly on my earlier note about NCT06993142.

Many teams find that proactive MIDD strategy reduces overall development time and strengthens regulatory interactions — especially in Parkinson Disease, Prodromal Stage where the regulatory landscape is evolving. Happy to share a relevant case study.

We recently supported a clinical development programme with PK/PD modelling that informed a key regulatory decision, reducing back-and-forth with FDA by several months — happy to share a short write-up if it'd be useful context for your team. No pitch, just the technical detail.

Would it be worth 15 minutes to see if the timing works for Cure Parkinson's?

Wishing you and the Cure Parkinson's team every success with NCT06993142.

contacts.notes:
Thanks for your email.
 
There is no pharmaceutical component in the innovative, prodromal exercise study in Parkinsons patients that you cited.
 
We have, however, launched perhaps 30-40 drug trials in patients over the past decade or more, and involving a lot of different biological targets, and therapeutic drug classes.
 
I am currently away from my desk but I'm happy to talk when I return.
-----------------------------------------------------------------
---Note - follow up on 29th April---
